subject.title: [优化建议] 添加结构化错误处理和智能重试机制

question: Which npm installer failures should OpenClaw auto-retry or auto-repair versus reporting with remediation guidance only?
rationale: The remaining source gap is real, but retrying network/TLS failures and rewriting npm prefix/PATH state can change setup behavior and trust boundaries across platforms.

options.title: Define narrow retry and repair policy
options.body: Retry only classified transient npm/network failures and add platform-specific remediation or safe repair for known permission failures, with Bash and PowerShell tests.

options.title: Improve diagnostics only
options.body: Keep install behavior unchanged while adding clear remediation text for common npm codes such as EACCES, ENOSPC, EBADENGINE, and certificate or network failures.

options.title: Keep current partial handling
options.body: Accept the existing code/syscall/errno output and targeted stale-directory/EEXIST cleanup retries without broader classification.

recommendation.title: Define narrow retry and repair policy
recommendation.body: Retry only classified transient npm/network failures and add platform-specific remediation or safe repair for known permission failures, with Bash and PowerShell tests.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent source-history signal across the Bash and PowerShell installer paths implicated by the decision.
